# Orderful — Style Reference

> Wire-drawn letters on white porcelain tiles, one red-hot rail. Hairline-weight Telegraf headlines sit on a #f5f5f5 grout of 8px-radius white tiles, with mono uppercase labels as the line work and a single orange-red gradient as the only heat.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Orderful speaks a tiled-bento infrastructure language. The page is a stack of white `#ffffff` tiles (57 background uses) set into a pale `#f5f5f5` body with 8px gutters, punctuated by one carbon `#1f1f1f` panel and ink `#000000` buttons. The chromatic budget is exactly one hue: the orange-red `#e42b0c`, rendered either solid or as a gradient from `#ff6a13`, and permitted only on the primary call to action, the hero and product illustrations, and one glowing nav pill. Typography carries the thesis. Telegraf headlines run at weight 100 and 300 across 48–72px with -0.025 to -0.03em tracking, so the largest words on the page are also the thinnest. Hierarchy comes from size jumps of roughly 1.2–1.25 and from mono uppercase micro-labels, while weight stays low. Shapes stay soft (4, 6 and 8px only), and elevation is almost entirely tonal: a white tile on grey grout, with one faint 1–3px shadow reserved for cards. The result reads as an engineering spec sheet rather than a sales brochure.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fog Canvas | `#f5f5f5` | `--color-fog-canvas` | Body background, the 8px grout between section tiles, and the frame behind the nav tiles. It makes every white tile read as a placed object rather than a stripe of page. |
| Paper Tile | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-tile` | Section tiles, product cards, nav tiles, inputs and logo cells, with 57 background uses. It is the workhorse surface, and it creates elevation by contrast with Fog Canvas alone. |
| Carbon Panel | `#1f1f1f` | `--color-carbon-panel` | The network-stats section, integration category labels (ERP, TMS/WMS, Platforms) and stat cells, with 9 uses. It is the single inverted mood shift on the page. Do not use it for more than one full-width section per page. |
| Ink | `#000000` | `--color-ink` | All headline and body text (73 uses), secondary button fills and the stat-grid frame. Pure black at thin weights keeps hairline strokes legible on white. |
| Slate Caption | `#4a5565` | `--color-slate-caption` | Product-card descriptions, hero sub-copy and integration blurbs. It is a cool grey that softens 14px running text so the 700-weight card titles lead. |
| Ash Caption | `#8a8a8a` | `--color-ash-caption` | Uppercase stat labels on Carbon Panel and other tertiary metadata, with 5 uses. It is the quietest text tone and is reserved for labels under numbers. |
| Pewter Border | `#d1d5dc` | `--color-pewter-border` | 1px hairlines on product cards, inputs, icon tiles and pagination squares, with 12 border uses. It defines edges without adding visual weight. |
| Ember Signal | `#e42b0c` | `--color-ember-signal` | Form submit fill, the end stop of the CTA gradient and the illustration grid lines. This is the entire chromatic budget. Never use it for body text or decorative borders. |
| Ember Flare | `#ff6a13` | `--color-ember-flare` | Estimated start stop of the "Get Started" and "Book a Demo" gradients and the warm highlights in product art. It exists only as half of a gradient. Do not use it as a standalone flat fill. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Telegraf — a geometric grotesk that does all display, body and UI work, with its signature at weights 100 and 300 · `--font-telegraf`

- **Substitute:** Inter Tight at 200 for the 100 cut and 300 for the 300 cut; Manrope at 300 for 300 and 200 for 100; Urbanist at 300. Telegraf's UltraLight 100 draws heavier than its number and renders closer to a 200, so do not pick a true hairline 100 that will look skeletal.
- **Weights:** 100, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14px, 16px, 18px, 20px, 24px, 30px, 48px, 60px, 72px
- **Line height:** 1.0 at 48–72px, 1.2 at 30px, 1.333 at 24px, 1.4 at 20px, 1.5 at 16px, 1.625 at 14px running text, 1.43 at 14px UI
- **Letter spacing:** -2.16px at 72px, -1.5px at 60px, -1.2px at 48px, -0.75px at 30px, -0.72px at 24px (400), -0.6px at 24px (700 and 100), -0.45px at 18px, 0.3px at 12px uppercase, 0.35px at 14px uppercase 600
- **OpenType features:** `case`
- **Role:** Telegraf runs light at large sizes. Most B2B SaaS sites push headlines to 600–700, while Orderful sets them at 100–300, and the brand reads as precise rather than loud. The display steps (72, 60, 48) follow a near Major Third (1.2–1.25), with a deliberate 1.6 leap from 48 down to 30 that separates headline from section label. Negative tracking holds at -0.025 to -0.03em on everything 18px and up so thin strokes still form tight word shapes. The `case` feature lifts punctuation for the uppercase micro-labels, which shows typographic care on otherwise utilitarian UI.

### modernGothic — a mono-flavoured uppercase micro-label face for nav and button text · `--font-modern-gothic`

- **Substitute:** DM Mono at 300, IBM Plex Mono at 300, Geist Mono at 300. modernGothic Light draws close to its nominal weight, so stay at 300 and avoid Space Mono, which only ships at 400 and reads heavier.
- **Weights:** 300
- **Sizes:** 14px
- **Line height:** 1.43
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 14px
- **OpenType features:** `ss02`
- **Role:** modernGothic appears only as 14px uppercase at weight 300 (9 uses), on nav tiles, "Book a Demo" and "View Success Stories". It is the technical voice of the system and nods to EDI's terminal heritage without dressing the page as a code editor. Pairing it with Telegraf gives a grotesk for statements and a mono for commands. The `ss02` alternate keeps the letterforms distinctive at small size.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Telegraf | 400 | 12px | 1.333 | 0.3px | `--text-small` |
| caption | modernGothic | 300 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Telegraf | 400 | 14px | 1.625 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Telegraf | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Telegraf | 400 | 20px | 1.4 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Telegraf | 400 | 24px | 1.333 | -0.72px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Telegraf | 700 | 24px | 1.333 | -0.6px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Telegraf | 300 | 30px | 1.2 | -0.75px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Telegraf | 300 | 60px | 1.0 | -1.5px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Telegraf | 300 | 72px | 1.0 | -2.16px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline from 48px to 72px at Telegraf weight 300 or 100 with -0.025 to -0.03em tracking (-2.16px at 72px) — thinness at scale is the signature and the source of the brand's calm authority.
- Build sections as separate `#ffffff` tiles with 8px radius on a `#f5f5f5` canvas with an 8px gutter — the grout line is the system's primary elevation device.
- Spend `#e42b0c` once per viewport, on the primary CTA or an illustration — a single hue on a neutral page draws the eye harder than three accents would.
- Set nav and button labels in modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase — the mono voice signals "command", separate from Telegraf's "statement".
- Use the 1px `#d1d5dc` hairline plus the `sm` shadow only on cards that hold product content — bordered cards then read as interactive objects against borderless section tiles.
- Keep radii to the closed set of 4px, 6px and 8px, tightening as elements get more precise (input 4px, button 6px, card 8px) — the radius ladder encodes function.
- Render metrics as Telegraf 30px weight 300 figures over 12px uppercase `#8a8a8a` labels with 0.3px tracking — light numerals keep data factual rather than shouty.

### Don't

- Don't bump display headlines to weight 600 or 700 to "add impact" — heavy 72px type overturns the thesis that authority here comes from hairline restraint, and it turns the page into a generic SaaS hero.
- Don't introduce a second hue such as a blue link or a purple badge alongside `#e42b0c` — the chromatic budget of one is non-negotiable, and a second color halves the CTA's pull.
- Don't use a flat `#ff6a13` fill anywhere — Ember Flare exists only as the start stop of the gradient, and alone it reads as a warning color.
- Don't run sections edge-to-edge in stripes of `#ffffff` and `#f5f5f5` — removing the 8px gutter and 8px radius erases the bento grammar the nav tiles set up.
- Don't add drop shadows deeper than the `sm` 1–3px blur to tiles or buttons — this system lifts through tone, and a 12px-blur card shadow looks pasted on.
- Don't use pill radii of 9999px on buttons — the system's largest radius is 8px, and pills read consumer-playful against EDI's precise register.
- Don't set body copy in modernGothic or labels in Telegraf at 14px weight 400 uppercase without tracking — never mix the two voices' jobs, because mono for paragraphs turns a sales page into a terminal dump.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #f5f5f5 (Fog Canvas)
- surface: #ffffff (Paper Tile)
- inverted panel: #1f1f1f (Carbon Panel)
- text: #000000 (Ink)
- secondary text: #4a5565 (Slate Caption)
- border: #d1d5dc (Pewter Border)
- primary action: #e42b0c (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts and metrics stay neutral, using `#000000`, `#1f1f1f` and `#8a8a8a` fills with `#d1d5dc` gridlines; `#e42b0c` may mark exactly one highlighted series or value, as a solid fill or as a 20% opacity tint for ranges, so the CTA remains the loudest object on the page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button: background `#e42b0c`, text `#ffffff`, no border, border-radius 6px, padding 8px 16px, font Telegraf 14px weight 500 uppercase, line-height 1.43, box-shadow `0px 1px 3px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.1), 0px 1px 2px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`. For the hero variant, replace the background with `linear-gradient(90deg, #ff6a13, #e42b0c)`, set the text to `#000000` in modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase, and add a trailing 12px dotted glyph with an 8px gap. Use only one per viewport.

2. Build a tiled navigation bar on a `#f5f5f5` background. Make it a horizontal row of separate tiles with an 8px gap, each `#ffffff` with border-radius 6px, 40px height and padding 0 16px, with labels in modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase `#000000`. Put a wider logo tile on the left. On the second tile, apply `box-shadow: inset 0 0 20px 0 rgba(243,43,9,0.4)`. Make the rightmost tile the gradient CTA (`#ff6a13` to `#e42b0c`) with `#000000` text. The bar is not sticky, and its max-width is 1440px.

3. Build a product card: background `#ffffff`, 1px solid `#d1d5dc` border, border-radius 8px, padding 32px, the `sm` shadow above. Stack its contents with a 16px gap: a 48px square icon tile (radius 6px, 1px `#d1d5dc` border) holding a 16px line icon, a Telegraf 24px weight 700 title at -0.6px letter-spacing in `#000000`, a 14px weight 400 description in `#4a5565` at line-height 1.625, a Telegraf 16px "Learn more" link in `#000000` with a trailing dotted glyph, and a gradient illustration image with radius 8px. Lay three of these in a 3-column grid with an 8px gap.

4. Build a network stats panel: a full-width tile with background `#1f1f1f`, radius 8px and padding 96px 64px. At the top, set a Telegraf 60px weight 300 headline in `#ffffff` at -1.5px letter-spacing, then 16px weight 400 body in `#8a8a8a` beneath it. Below that, place a 5-column grid inside a `#000000` frame with 4px padding and a 4px gap, with cells in `#1f1f1f`, radius 6px and padding 16px. Each cell holds a Telegraf 30px weight 300 figure in `#ffffff` and a 12px weight 400 uppercase label in `#8a8a8a` at 0.3px tracking. Right-align a button pair with an 8px gap: one with a `#ffffff` fill and `#000000` text, and one transparent with a 1px `#ffffff` border, both radius 6px, padding 8px 16px, modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase.

5. Build a split hero as two `#ffffff` tiles side by side on `#f5f5f5` with an 8px gap, each with radius 8px. The left tile has padding 64px and holds a Telegraf 72px weight 300 headline in `#000000`, with line-height 1.0, -2.16px letter-spacing and 24px bottom padding. Below it, add a 24px weight 400 subheading at -0.72px in `#4a5565`, then a 32px gap and the gradient primary button. The right tile holds a full-bleed illustration with no padding.

| Element | Value |

| sections | 8px |

## Components

### Tiled Navigation Bar

**Role:** Primary site navigation as separate tiles

The system outlier is the "AI-native EDI" pill, a tile tinted with the `sm-2` inset glow of 20px orange-red, which is allowed because it marks the one product claim the brand wants scanned first. Breaking the bar into tiles previews the bento grammar of the page below.

### Gradient Action Button — Ember (Primary)

**Role:** Conversion CTA: demo, start, submit

The only warm object. The solid form-submit variant measures `#e42b0c` fill, `#ffffff` text, no border, 6px radius, 8px 16px padding, and Telegraf 14px weight 500 uppercase with the `sm` shadow. The hero and nav variants swap the flat fill for a left-to-right gradient from `#ff6a13` to `#e42b0c`, set `#000000` modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase, and add a trailing dotted glyph. One per viewport is the rule, because Ember is the page's entire chromatic budget.

### Ink Button — Secondary

**Role:** Secondary navigation into proof content

Black, flat, technical. The fill is `#000000` with `#ffffff` text, no border, 6px radius, 8px 16px padding and an estimated 40px height, set in modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase with a trailing dotted glyph. It carries no shadow. It appears under the G2 block ("View Success Stories") and the integrations block ("Talk to an Expert"). Ink rather than an outline is the anti-convention move here: the secondary button has full contrast but zero hue, so it never competes with Ember.

### Ghost Button on Carbon — Inverse Pair

**Role:** Paired actions on the dark panel

Mirrored pair. The leading button fills `#ffffff` with `#000000` text, while its sibling is transparent with a 1px `#ffffff` border and `#ffffff` text. Both use 6px radius, 8px 16px padding, modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase and an 8px gap between them, and both are right-aligned under the stat grid. The white border appears only here (2 uses), which keeps hairline-white as a Carbon-only device rather than a general outline style.

### Section Tile

**Role:** Full-width bento container per section

The structural brick. Each tile is a `#ffffff` field at 8px radius, with no border and no shadow, separated from its neighbours by 8px of `#f5f5f5` grout. Internal padding runs 64px on compact rows and 96px on hero and headline rows, and content is held to 1280px inside a 1440px frame. One tile per section swaps to `#1f1f1f` for the network panel. Stacking separate tiles in place of the conventional edge-to-edge stripe makes the page feel assembled from modules, which suits a product about connecting systems.

### Product Card

**Role:** Platform product summary with illustration

Bordered, barely lifted. The card is `#ffffff` with a 1px `#d1d5dc` border, 8px radius, 32px padding and the `sm` shadow. Inside it sits a 48px icon tile (6px radius, 1px `#d1d5dc` border), then a Telegraf 24px weight 700 title at -0.6px, then 14px weight 400 copy in `#4a5565` at 1.625, then a 16px "Learn more" link with a dotted glyph, and finally an 8px-radius orange gradient illustration. The 700 title is the system's heaviest common weight, set beside hairline section headlines on purpose: card titles are labels, not statements.

### Carbon Stat Cell

**Role:** Network metrics on dark panel

Terminal readout. A row of five cells sits inside a `#000000` frame with 4px gaps showing between the `#1f1f1f` cells. Each cell has 6px radius and 16px padding. It holds a dotted up-arrow glyph (a decorative green, not a system token), a Telegraf 30px weight 300 figure in `#ffffff`, and a 12px weight 400 uppercase label in `#8a8a8a` at 0.3px tracking. Thin numerals at 30px read as measured data rather than as marketing hyperbole.

### Integration Matrix

**Role:** Partner logos grouped by category

Grid with a dark index column. A 4-column, 3-row matrix sits on a `#f5f5f5` well with 4px gaps. Category cells in the first column fill `#1f1f1f` and carry `#ffffff` Telegraf 20px weight 300 labels (ERP, TMS/WMS, Platforms). Logo cells are `#ffffff` with 1px `#d1d5dc` hairlines, and every cell uses a 6px radius. It reads like a database table with the key column inverted, which suits an EDI audience fluent in schemas.

### Logo Wall

**Role:** Social proof marquee strip

Monochrome, unboxed. A Telegraf 24px weight 100 heading at -0.6px ("Trusted by the World's Leading Brands") sits above a horizontally scrolling row of customer marks at a fixed 40px height, all rendered in `#000000` with 64px between marks and no cards or borders. Weight 100 here is the thinnest text on the page, so the logos rather than the label do the talking.

### Industry Tab Rail

**Role:** Vertical industry selector

Tall vertical tabs. Each tab is a narrow, full-height column with transparent background, `#000000` text, 8px radius and 32px 16px padding, set in Telegraf 16px weight 400 (Logistics, Food & Beverage, Manufacturing, SaaS & Tech Platforms, Carriers). The active tab expands its panel horizontally. It replaces the conventional horizontal tab strip with an accordion-like rail, which suits five long category names.

### Form Input

**Role:** Demo-request field

Plain and squared. The input is `#ffffff` with `#000000` text, a 1px `#d1d5dc` border, 4px radius and 16px padding, set in Telegraf 12px weight 400, with no shadow. It pairs with the solid Ember submit button. The 4px radius is a step tighter than buttons at 6px and cards at 8px, so data-entry surfaces read as the most precise objects in the system.

### Pagination Square

**Role:** Carousel and testimonial stepping

Small square chips. Each chip is a 40px square with `#ffffff` fill and 1px `#d1d5dc` border when inactive, and a transparent borderless state when active. Chips use 4px radius and Telegraf 14px weight 400 numerals in `#000000`. They share the input radius on purpose: anything you click to step through data takes the tightest corner.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline from 48px to 72px at Telegraf weight 300 or 100 with -0.025 to -0.03em tracking (-2.16px at 72px) — thinness at scale is the signature and the source of the brand's calm authority.
- Build sections as separate `#ffffff` tiles with 8px radius on a `#f5f5f5` canvas with an 8px gutter — the grout line is the system's primary elevation device.
- Spend `#e42b0c` once per viewport, on the primary CTA or an illustration — a single hue on a neutral page draws the eye harder than three accents would.
- Set nav and button labels in modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase — the mono voice signals "command", separate from Telegraf's "statement".
- Use the 1px `#d1d5dc` hairline plus the `sm` shadow only on cards that hold product content — bordered cards then read as interactive objects against borderless section tiles.
- Keep radii to the closed set of 4px, 6px and 8px, tightening as elements get more precise (input 4px, button 6px, card 8px) — the radius ladder encodes function.
- Render metrics as Telegraf 30px weight 300 figures over 12px uppercase `#8a8a8a` labels with 0.3px tracking — light numerals keep data factual rather than shouty.

### Don't

- Don't bump display headlines to weight 600 or 700 to "add impact" — heavy 72px type overturns the thesis that authority here comes from hairline restraint, and it turns the page into a generic SaaS hero.
- Don't introduce a second hue such as a blue link or a purple badge alongside `#e42b0c` — the chromatic budget of one is non-negotiable, and a second color halves the CTA's pull.
- Don't use a flat `#ff6a13` fill anywhere — Ember Flare exists only as the start stop of the gradient, and alone it reads as a warning color.
- Don't run sections edge-to-edge in stripes of `#ffffff` and `#f5f5f5` — removing the 8px gutter and 8px radius erases the bento grammar the nav tiles set up.
- Don't add drop shadows deeper than the `sm` 1–3px blur to tiles or buttons — this system lifts through tone, and a 12px-blur card shadow looks pasted on.
- Don't use pill radii of 9999px on buttons — the system's largest radius is 8px, and pills read consumer-playful against EDI's precise register.
- Don't set body copy in modernGothic or labels in Telegraf at 14px weight 400 uppercase without tracking — never mix the two voices' jobs, because mono for paragraphs turns a sales page into a terminal dump.

## Surfaces

| Level | Name | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Fog Canvas | `#f5f5f5` | Body and gutter grout behind every tile |
| 1 | Paper Tile | `#ffffff` | Section tiles, nav tiles, cards, inputs, logo cells |
| 2 | Carbon Panel | `#1f1f1f` | The single inverted network section and matrix category cells |
| 3 | Ink | `#000000` | Secondary button fills and the stat-grid frame, the deepest inversion |

## Elevation

- **Product cards and form submit button:** `0px 1px 3px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), 0px 1px 2px -1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)`
- **"AI-native EDI" nav pill (sole glow, decorative emphasis):** `inset 0px 0px 20px 0px rgba(243, 43, 9, 0.4)`

Everything else is tonal: white `#ffffff` tiles lift off `#f5f5f5` grout, and `#1f1f1f` sinks below both. Shadows are rationed to 5 elements on the entire page.

## Imagery

Imagery is illustration, not photography. Product art abstracts the UI as stylised interface fragments (an API key panel, a purchase order table, a shipping label with barcode) floating over orange-to-red gradients built from pixelated mosaic squares, all framed in 8px-radius images with no border or shadow. The hero pairs a black slab carrying the white Orderful wordmark with a red-lined grid of retailer logos (Amazon, Kroger, Kohl's, Target) and flowchart nodes labelled in mono uppercase, wired by a glowing red rail. Customer logos are flat monochrome black. G2 award badges and a single customer headshot are the only external raster assets. Icons are small line glyphs inside 48px bordered tiles, and a dotted "loading" glyph trails every button label. The gradient is decorative art, not a surface token, and never backs text blocks. The narrative is a network lighting up: data flowing through a red-hot pipeline into a grid of trading partners.

## Layout

The frame is 1440px wide, with content held to 1280px, and every section is its own 8px-radius white tile stacked on an 8px `#f5f5f5` gutter. Section padding runs 64–96px inside tiles. The hero splits into two tiles side by side: a left tile with a 72px weight-300 headline, 24px sub-copy and the gradient CTA, and a right tile holding a full-bleed illustration. After the hero, sections alternate between centered headline-over-grid rows (the 3-column product cards) and asymmetric splits (headline left, G2 badges or the integration matrix right). One `#1f1f1f` tile breaks the rhythm with a 5-column stat row. Logos run as a single scrolling row. The nav is static: a left logo tile, label tiles, and a right gradient CTA tile, each about 40px tall. The footer is a wide multi-column link sitemap headed by mono uppercase labels. At 375px, drop the display to 48px, collapse grids to 1 column, and keep the 8px gutter with 48px tile padding. Density: comfortable.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #f5f5f5 (Fog Canvas)
- surface: #ffffff (Paper Tile)
- inverted panel: #1f1f1f (Carbon Panel)
- text: #000000 (Ink)
- secondary text: #4a5565 (Slate Caption)
- border: #d1d5dc (Pewter Border)
- primary action: #e42b0c (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts and metrics stay neutral, using `#000000`, `#1f1f1f` and `#8a8a8a` fills with `#d1d5dc` gridlines; `#e42b0c` may mark exactly one highlighted series or value, as a solid fill or as a 20% opacity tint for ranges, so the CTA remains the loudest object on the page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button: background `#e42b0c`, text `#ffffff`, no border, border-radius 6px, padding 8px 16px, font Telegraf 14px weight 500 uppercase, line-height 1.43, box-shadow `0px 1px 3px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.1), 0px 1px 2px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`. For the hero variant, replace the background with `linear-gradient(90deg, #ff6a13, #e42b0c)`, set the text to `#000000` in modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase, and add a trailing 12px dotted glyph with an 8px gap. Use only one per viewport.

2. Build a tiled navigation bar on a `#f5f5f5` background. Make it a horizontal row of separate tiles with an 8px gap, each `#ffffff` with border-radius 6px, 40px height and padding 0 16px, with labels in modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase `#000000`. Put a wider logo tile on the left. On the second tile, apply `box-shadow: inset 0 0 20px 0 rgba(243,43,9,0.4)`. Make the rightmost tile the gradient CTA (`#ff6a13` to `#e42b0c`) with `#000000` text. The bar is not sticky, and its max-width is 1440px.

3. Build a product card: background `#ffffff`, 1px solid `#d1d5dc` border, border-radius 8px, padding 32px, the `sm` shadow above. Stack its contents with a 16px gap: a 48px square icon tile (radius 6px, 1px `#d1d5dc` border) holding a 16px line icon, a Telegraf 24px weight 700 title at -0.6px letter-spacing in `#000000`, a 14px weight 400 description in `#4a5565` at line-height 1.625, a Telegraf 16px "Learn more" link in `#000000` with a trailing dotted glyph, and a gradient illustration image with radius 8px. Lay three of these in a 3-column grid with an 8px gap.

4. Build a network stats panel: a full-width tile with background `#1f1f1f`, radius 8px and padding 96px 64px. At the top, set a Telegraf 60px weight 300 headline in `#ffffff` at -1.5px letter-spacing, then 16px weight 400 body in `#8a8a8a` beneath it. Below that, place a 5-column grid inside a `#000000` frame with 4px padding and a 4px gap, with cells in `#1f1f1f`, radius 6px and padding 16px. Each cell holds a Telegraf 30px weight 300 figure in `#ffffff` and a 12px weight 400 uppercase label in `#8a8a8a` at 0.3px tracking. Right-align a button pair with an 8px gap: one with a `#ffffff` fill and `#000000` text, and one transparent with a 1px `#ffffff` border, both radius 6px, padding 8px 16px, modernGothic 14px weight 300 uppercase.

5. Build a split hero as two `#ffffff` tiles side by side on `#f5f5f5` with an 8px gap, each with radius 8px. The left tile has padding 64px and holds a Telegraf 72px weight 300 headline in `#000000`, with line-height 1.0, -2.16px letter-spacing and 24px bottom padding. Below it, add a 24px weight 400 subheading at -0.72px in `#4a5565`, then a 32px gap and the gradient primary button. The right tile holds a full-bleed illustration with no padding.

## Hairline Display Discipline

The defining discipline is that the largest type is the lightest. Display and heading-lg run at weight 300, the logo-wall and G2 headings drop to 100, and only 24px card titles climb to 700. The scale inverts the conventional rule that size and weight rise together. Three things would break it: a 600-weight hero, tracking relaxed to 0 at 60px and above (thin strokes then drift apart), or a substitute font that renders a true skeletal 100 and looks faint on `#ffffff`. To extend the system, give any new statement headline of 30px or more weight 300 with -0.025em tracking, and any new label 24px or smaller weight 500–700. A new hierarchy level should come from size steps of roughly 1.2–1.25 rather than from added weight.

## Tile Gutter Grammar

The page is assembled from tiles, and every tile is separated by 8px of `#f5f5f5`. The nav announces this grammar by splitting into individual 6px-radius tiles, then the sections, product cards, stat cells and integration matrix repeat it at smaller scales with 4–8px gaps. The grammar breaks when sections bleed edge-to-edge, when the gutter widens to a conventional 64px whitespace band, or when tiles pick up borders and deep shadows that duplicate the job the grout already does. To extend it, place new content inside a new `#ffffff` tile at 8px radius, nest sub-modules on a `#f5f5f5` well with 4px gaps, and let tone rather than lines define every edge.

## One-Hue Heat

The palette holds one hue. `#e42b0c` and its gradient partner `#ff6a13` are the only saturated colors in the system, and they appear on a single CTA per viewport, inside illustrations, and as one inset glow on the nav. Everything else is `#000000`, `#1f1f1f`, `#4a5565`, `#8a8a8a`, `#d1d5dc` and white. The budget breaks with a second brand hue, with orange used as link text or decorative borders, or with gradient backdrops behind paragraphs. The stat arrows' green is decorative art, not a status system. To extend the palette, express new states through Ink weight changes and Pewter hairlines, and reserve Ember for the single thing a visitor should do next.

## Similar Brands

- **Orderful** — Shares Vercel's black-and-white neutral stack with mono uppercase micro-labels on buttons, but adds a warm orange-red gradient where Vercel stays achromatic.
- **Orderful** — Shares Stedi's developer-facing EDI positioning and product-UI-as-illustration approach, but swaps Stedi's dense documentation feel for 72px hairline headlines and bento tiles.
- **Orderful** — Shares SPS Commerce's category (retail EDI networks and trading-partner logo grids), but replaces the incumbent's heavy corporate blue and bold headings with a one-hue, weight-300 system.
- **Orderful** — Shares Ramp's single-accent discipline on a neutral canvas with tightly tracked display type, though Ramp's headlines sit at medium weight where Orderful's sit at 100–300.
- **Orderful** — Shares Apple's product-page bento grammar of rounded tiles on a light grey field, applied to B2B infrastructure with 8px rather than 18px-plus corners.
